items.title: Inject #1 - Spoofed IT call for account access
items.body:
If the reps has identified that their accounts are compromised, once escalated to TL,
- An IT ticket will be created for Corporate Security to Investigate
- An incident ticket will be created on the client side, inform via Program’s internal Chat providing the INC ticket number
- send an email to Client’s phishing reporting channel

items.title: Inject #2 - Unauthorized access detected
items.body: After containment, blocking of IP and Domain of the login attempts, Logs will be reviewed for any other attack vectors or ongoing attacks. Accounts are flagged and block with in-placed security controls. Further investigation will be conducted, review logs and interview the affected account user.

items.title: Decision A - Contain the breach
items.body:
Q1: Once ticket has been created and account/s has been identified, it will be isolated, pw reset and trace/check logs for any compromise/attacks

Q2: L1 - initial assessment of BI, Ops team has cross/up skilled reps to distribute workload
Sales - will be distributing workloads to active reps and solicit OT
L2 - taps specialized/skilled trained rep to increase volume and workload distribution

Q3: Logs will be reviewed. IP and domains will be blocked and check logs from IP and Domain for any attack vectors or ongoing attacks

Q4: Ops Leader will create the Ticket notifying both Internal IT and Client IT, with communication to the Client about the incident

items.title: Decision B - Operations recovery
items.body:
Q1: Ops and Security Team are coordinating in restoring operation without high potential business impact. Operations has BC plan and operational protocols to eliminate any impact.

Q2: The Ops team has verification protocols in place following non-customer related calls coming through the customer hotline

Q3: Cybersecurity Awareness training, Courses in KB and reinforcement through posting in Sharepoint

Q4: Reinforcement of awareness and constant reminders with reps. Continuing education and awareness training is being conducted. Security team conducts Phishing tests to test employee awareness.

scenario.title: Vishing Attack
scenario.kicker: Social engineering attack targeting customer care staff to obtain account access

objectives.title: Objectives & ground rules
items: Test the customer care team's ability to identify and report spoofed IT calls
Evaluate account security procedures and escalation protocols
Assess operational impact on service delivery during a security incident
Review incident communication and client notification processes

data.ground_rules: Stay in role. No wrong answers — this is a discussion, not a test. Call out what you don't know. Every decision gets an Annex A control.

data.text: Would our customer care team challenge a spoofed IT call? What is our verification ritual?

slides.name: After Action Executive Summary

data.participants: Operations Manager, Team Leaders, Customer Care Agents, IT Security, Compliance, HR
highlights: Customer care agent fell victim to social engineering and provided account credentials
Security detected unauthorized access from unknown location within 25 minutes
Data export attempt was blocked by DLP controls before customer data was exfiltrated
Verification protocol was not followed — no challenge to caller identity
lessons: Caller verification needs a formal ritual — not just good intentions
Customer care teams need regular social engineering awareness training
Operational impact assessment must be immediate — agent queue redistribution
Client notification criteria need to be clear and contractual
data.story: The exercise unfolded through the following injects: At 14:10, Spoofed IT call for account access — A customer care agent received a call from someone claiming to be from internal IT support, requesting account verification for a 'system migration.' The agent provided login credentials and answered security questions. At 14:35, Unauthorized access detected — Security alerts flagged login attempts from an unknown location. The attacker had accessed customer records and was attempting to export data. The hotwash closed on a single question: Would our customer care team challenge a spoofed IT call? What is our verification ritual? Every decision was mapped to an ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A control, and the exercise ended with a set of owned follow-up actions.
recommendations: Prioritise: Implement IT support call verification protocol (A.6.3) — owner: IT Security
Prioritise: Add social engineering training for customer care teams (A.7.2) — owner: HR
Prioritise: Deploy account monitoring for unauthorized location access (A.8.15) — owner: IT Security
Prioritise: Establish client notification criteria and escalation matrix (A.5.20) — owner: Compliance

decisions: Approve a funded remediation program for caller verification, social engineering training, account monitoring, and client notification.
Designate a single operations owner for CAPA governance and monthly reporting until all high-priority items are closed.
Require customer care teams to complete social engineering awareness training within 30 days.
Require a follow-up tabletop exercise within 180 days to verify improvement.
evidence: Incident declaration, severity classification, and time-stamped decision log.
Account access logs, login attempt records, and unauthorized location evidence.
DLP alerts, data export attempts, and blocked transfer evidence.
Caller verification protocol test results and training completion records.
Client notification records and escalation matrix documentation.
Recovery and improvement evidence: account reset, session revocation, and CAPA closure.

roadmap.milestones: Assign owners; publish war-room RACI; approve containment thresholds; update legal/privacy notification matrix; complete privileged-account inventory; implement priority SIEM alerts.
Deploy or tune PAM/JIT controls; complete detection engineering; exercise exfiltration response; execute forensic evidence tabletop.
Validate recovery gates and restore drills; run follow-up tabletop; close CAPA evidence; update control narratives and evidence repository.
